title: The Rediscovery of Zamzam and the Vow of Abdul Muttalib
overview: This episode details the rediscovery of the lost well of Zamzam by Abdul Muttalib following a series of divine dreams and specific physical clues. It covers the dispute between Abdul Muttalib and Quraysh over custodianship, which was resolved by a miraculous emergence of water in the desert during their journey to an arbitrator. Finally, the lecture explains Abdul Muttalib's vow to sacrifice one of his sons, the selection of Abdullah through lots, and his eventual ransom with one hundred camels.
lessons: Divine guidance often comes to those who remain steadfast in their duties, as seen in the dreams granted to Abdul Muttalib.
True leadership demands dignity, resilience, and proactiveness during crises rather than passive acceptance of defeat.
Generosity toward one's opponents in times of mutual hardship can soften hearts and resolve bitter conflicts.
Rash oaths made out of tribal pride or emotional strain can lead to severe trials, underscoring Islam's strict prohibition of harmful vows and human sacrifice.
Divine Decree (Qadar) continuously protects the sacred lineage of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, ensuring that both Ismail and Abdullah were spared from sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Dreams of Abdul Muttalib
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib, the grandfather of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, held the prestigious duty of providing water and refreshments to pilgrims visiting Makkah, a role inherited through the noble line of Abd Manaf and Qusayy ibn Kilab. Over four consecutive nights, he experienced vivid dreams in which a voice repeatedly commanded him to dig, initially offering cryptic names before specifically identifying the well of Zamzam. The voice provided three physical clues to pinpoint the precise location of the long-buried well near the Ka'bah. Accompanied by his eldest and then-only adult son, al-Harith, Abdul Muttalib set out to investigate these signs.
key_points: Abdul Muttalib inherited the responsibility of water provision (siqayah) from the lineage of Abd Manaf.
Four names were revealed in consecutive dreams: Tibah, Barrah, al-Madmunah, and Zamzam.
The dream provided three specific location clues: between intestines and blood, at an ant colony, and where a white-feathered crow pecks.
Al-Harith was Abdul Muttalib's only adult son available to assist him at the time.

chapters.title: Uncovering the Well of Zamzam
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib observed a cow being sacrificed near the idol Isaf, which fulfilled the clue regarding blood and animal intestines when the cow broke loose and collapsed. Searching the vicinity, he located both an ant colony and a black crow with a single white wing feather (al-ghurab al-a'sam) pecking the earth. As Abdul Muttalib began digging at the site, Quraysh leaders attempted to stop him, but his son al-Harith distracted the crowd. Upon reaching the original stone lining of the well, Abdul Muttalib proclaimed 'Allahu Akbar' as fresh water gushed forth, confirming the recovery of Zamzam.
key_points: Sacrifice of a cow near the idol Isaf fulfilled the sign of blood and intestines (bayna al-rafthi wa-ad-dam).
A crow with a white feather in its wing (al-Ghurab al-A'sam) pecking near an ant colony marked the exact spot.
Al-Harith kept the opposing Quraysh members at bay while his father excavated.
Reaching the well's original stone masonry confirmed the location, prompting Abdul Muttalib to shout the takbir.

chapters.title: The Dispute over Ownership and the Desert Journey
chapters.summary: Following the discovery of Zamzam, the leaders of Quraysh demanded equal partnership in the well, arguing it was a shared legacy from their ancestor Ismail (peace be upon him). Abdul Muttalib firmly refused, asserting that the discovery and custodianship were granted exclusively to him and his immediate family. To resolve the high-stakes dispute, both parties agreed to travel to Yathrib and Khaybar to consult a renowned soothsayer, Kahinah Bani Sa'd. During the arduous journey through the desert, Abdul Muttalib's group ran completely out of water and prepared for death by digging their own graves.
key_points: Quraysh demanded shared rights to Zamzam as descendants of Prophet Ismail (alayhis-salam).
Abdul Muttalib refused to surrender sole custodianship of the well he personally excavated.
Both parties agreed to seek arbitration from Kahinah Bani Sa'd in Yathrib and Khaybar.
Facing severe dehydration in the desert, Abdul Muttalib's group dug their own graves to preserve their dignity.

chapters.title: Miracle in the Desert and Resolution of Custodianship
chapters.summary: Refusing to succumb to passive despair in their graves, Abdul Muttalib encouraged his men to make a final effort to search for water. As his camel rose and struck its hoof on the ground, a miraculous spring of fresh water gushed forth from the dry earth. Demonstrating nobility, Abdul Muttalib shared the water with his Quraysh rivals who had previously denied him their own supplies. Overwhelmed by this divine sign, Quraysh conceded that the Lord who provided water in the desert was the same One who granted him Zamzam, yielding complete custodianship to Abdul Muttalib.
key_points: Abdul Muttalib urged his companions to actively search for life rather than await death in their graves.
Water gushed from beneath the hoof of Abdul Muttalib's camel in the middle of the barren desert.
Abdul Muttalib generously invited his opponents to drink and replenish their water supplies.
Quraysh recognized divine intervention, withdrew their legal claim, and granted Abdul Muttalib sole rights to Zamzam.

chapters.title: The Vow of Abdul Muttalib and the Ransom of Abdullah
chapters.summary: During the initial excavation of Zamzam, feeling vulnerable with only one son, Abdul Muttalib had vowed to sacrifice one son to Allah if he were granted ten. Years later, after fathering ten sons—including al-Abbas, Hamzah, Abu Talib, Abu Lahab, and Abdullah—he prepared to fulfill his vow by casting divining arrows at the Ka'bah. The lot repeatedly selected his most beloved son, Abdullah, the father of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Quraysh intervened to prevent human sacrifice from becoming an established custom, sending him to Kahinah Bani Sa'd. She instructed casting lots between Abdullah and ten camels, increasing the count by ten each time Abdullah was selected, until one hundred camels were finally chosen by the arrows, ransoming Abdullah.
key_points: Abdul Muttalib had ten sons: al-Harith, al-Zubayr, Hajl, al-Muqawwim, Dirar, al-Abbas, Hamzah, Abu Talib, Abu Lahab, and Abdullah.
Only al-Abbas and Hamzah embraced Islam, while Abu Talib and Abu Lahab lived to see Islam but died in disbelief.
Divining arrows (azlam) repeatedly selected Abdullah to be sacrificed at the idol Isaf.
Quraysh stopped the sacrifice to prevent establishing a harmful precedent (sunnah) among Arabs.
One hundred camels were slaughtered as blood money (diyah) to redeem Abdullah.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ referred to himself as 'the son of the two sacrificed ones' (Ismail and Abdullah).

segments.translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-ʿālamīn, wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihī wa ṣaḥbihī ajmaʿīn. Wa baʿd.

segments.text: Last week, we left off talking about the story of the [[Quraysh|قريش]] and how they re-controlled or regained control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
and how from the lineage of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] came the grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ,
whose name was actually [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]], but he became well-known as [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], and [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] is the name that stuck with him.
So he came back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] when he reached the age of adolescence,
and eventually the responsibilities of taking care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]] in terms of providing them with drink, it came to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
Because [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was from the lineage of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]],

and [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] was the son of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] who was given the responsibility of providing drink for the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], providing water for the [[hujjaj|حجاج]].
And it went on to the sons of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], and then to their sons,
and it went eventually to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] who was the grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
Now, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], his first son was named al-Harith.
This was the first son of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]. Later on, he had many more sons, he had a total of 10 sons, but his firstborn son was al-Harith.
Now, when al-Harith grew to an age of adolescence, when he became a strong young man,
[[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] saw a dream. He saw a dream.
And in this dream, a voice came to him in the dream and said to him,
And then [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] asked,
"What is Ṭībah?" And there was no answer, and the voice went away.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] thought about this dream, and he wondered what it meant.
The next night, the voice came to him again in his dream.
And this time, the voice said to him,
And then [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] asked the voice,
"What is Barrah?" And there was no answer from the voice, and the voice went away.
The third night, again he had a dream, a voice saying to him,
And then [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] asked the voice,
"What is al-Maḍmūnah?" And there was no answer from the voice, and the voice went away. So this went on for three nights.
The fourth night,
the fourth night he had a dream again with the voice saying to him,
And then [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] asked,
"What is [[Zamzam|زمزم]]?"
And then the voice said to him in the dream,

segments.translit: Lā tanzifu abadan wa lā tarum, tasqil-ḥajjājal-aʿẓam, wa hiya baynar-rafthi wad-dam, ʿinda naqratil-ghurābil-aʿṣam, ʿinda qaryatin-naml.

segments.text: So they explained, the voice explained to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] where he could find
the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] with these few lines.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] remembered the words that he heard in this dream.
Now, the caller in the dream didn't tell him the exact location where the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was, but
some signs were given. Some signs were given, and those signs were three signs.
The [[Zamzam|زمزم]], you will find it between ar-rafth and ad-dam. Ar-rafth is used to describe
the intestines of an animal. The intestines of an animal is called ar-rafth. And ad-dam is blood.
So this is the first clue that was given to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] in the dream about the location of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]. It is between the intestines of the animal and the blood.
Okay, you might think this is strange. Where are you going to find intestines of an animal and blood, you know, in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] near the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]?
So that was the first sign. The second sign was
In the place where al-ghurāb al-aʿṣam... And al-ghurāb al-aʿṣam is a crow, and you know what color is a crow, a crow is black.
So al-ghurāb, it means a crow, and a crow is known to be black. But al-ghurāb al-aʿṣam,
this is what the Arabs used to call a crow that was black, but it had a white feather in the wing.
A crow is usually completely black, but if you find a crow that's all black, but there's one white feather in the wing,
this is what the Arabs used to call al-ghurāb al-aʿṣam, the crow with a white feather in the wing.
So this is the second clue. Where the crow with the white feather in its wing pecks,
So it is between the intestines of the animal and the blood, it is in a place where the crow with whiteness in its wing pecks.
At the ant colony, where the ants have made a village, or where the ants have made a colony.
So these were the three signs that were given to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] in the dream as where to find [[Zamzam|زمزم]].
Now, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and the people who lived in his time, they had never seen [[Zamzam|زمزم]] before, but they knew what [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was.
Because they knew the story of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]. They knew that their forefathers had settled in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] because of [[Zamzam|زمزم]].
And they knew that when the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] overtook the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
before [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was overtaken, they buried that well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] so that [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] could not benefit from it.
So they knew about this story.
They knew that [[Zamzam|زمزم]] existed, and they knew the story of [[Zamzam|زمزم]], and they knew the story of why the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was buried by their forefathers.
But why didn't they go around looking for it? Even though they knew it existed, why didn't they go around looking for it? Because they didn't know where to look for it.
They knew it was there somewhere in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], but you think they're going to go digging around all of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] looking for that well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]?
No, of course they can't do that.
But now [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] in this dream, the location was narrowed down to him by these three clues.
So he thought, "Okay, maybe I have a chance. Maybe I can actually narrow it down, and I can finally find the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] again."
And what a great honor that would be!
What a great honor that would be. So he decided to try to follow the clues that he saw in his dream.
And he took his son with him, al-Harith. And al-Harith was the only one of his sons at that time who had reached an age of strength. He was a young man,
and he could actually help his father out. As for the other children, they were still little.
You know, he didn't have anyone else who could really go with him and work with him. So he took his son al-Harith,
and he went there to the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. And he was thinking about the first sign:
It is between the intestines of the animal and the blood. So he was thinking, "Where am I going to find this?"
And at that point, somebody or a group of people had come to the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]],
and we know that at this time the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] had idols inside it, the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] had idols around it.
And two of those idols that were near the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] were [[Isaf|إساف]] and [[Na'ilah|نائلة]], and we spoke about them in a previous lesson.
[[Isaf|إساف]] and [[Na'ilah|نائلة]], they were those two people, the boy and the girl who had come from [[Yemen|اليمن]],
and they were doing immoral actions in the [[Haram|حرم]] itself, and Allah Almighty caused them to turn into stone.
and when [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]] brought idol worship back into the [[Jazirat al-Arab|جَزِيرَة الْعَرَب]],
he took these two stones of [[Isaf|إساف]] and [[Na'ilah|نائلة]] and put them in front of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So people would go there and they would actually offer sacrifices there, and they would worship those stones.
So this continued until the time of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], it was still going on, people were still worshipping the idols.
So when [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] came with his son to start his search for the lost well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]],
a group of people came to the idol of [[Isaf|إساف]] with a cow.
And they were going to sacrifice that cow to [[Isaf|إساف]], to the idol. They were going to slaughter that cow as a sacrifice to this idol.
So they started sacrificing the cow, they started cutting it, slaughtering it. So they cut the neck, and the blood started pouring out of the neck.
So the blood was all over the ground there.
But the cow, it was a bit strong, so it was able to get loose even though it was bleeding and it was hurt.
It was able to get loose, and it jumped up and it started running with blood dripping all from it.
But of course, you know, it was weakened because of the blood loss. So eventually a little bit as it ran, you know, maybe for some time, then it fell down again.
And then they caught it again, and they were able to overpower it, and they completed cutting it. And they cut open the stomach as well.
and the intestines fell out.
The intestines of that cow fell out onto the ground. And [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]], he saw all of this happen.
So he saw the blood come out in the first place, and then the cow ran, and they completed the slaughter, and they cut open the stomach, and the intestines fell out.
So he said, "This is the first clue."
It is between the intestines and the blood. So he saw the location where the blood started to come out, and he saw the location where the intestines came out.
So he said, "Okay, that narrows it down somewhat. It's between this place and this place."
But that place was still pretty big. It's not like it was a very precise location he could go start digging now. No, that was still a pretty big area.
Not as big as the whole [[Makkah|مَكَٜة]], of course, so it was narrowed down definitely, but still not narrow enough for him to actually start his work in digging.
So he started looking around that narrowed-down area now for the other two clues:
Where the crow with the whiteness in its wing is pecking, and where the ant colony is. So he looked around, and he found an ant colony in that area.
He did find an ant colony.
But of course, the ant colony, it wasn't very small either. It was a pretty big ant colony, and it wasn't enough for him to actually start digging.
It narrowed it down much more, yes, but still not enough for him to start digging.
And then, a crow came down. A crow came down, and he noticed that this crow actually had whiteness—one of the feathers of the wing was white.
So he said, "This is [[al-Ghurab al-A'sam|الْغُرَاب الْأَعْصَم]]." And it came down near the ant colony, and it started pecking the ground.
So he said, "This is it. This is as narrow as it can get. The crow is in one location, and it is actually pecking there.
That is where I need to dig. That's where I'm going to find the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]."
So he knew that these three clues had led him to the exact location. So he started to dig.
And remember, this is all a big public place right in front of the [[Ka'bah|كعة]]. So it's not like he can do it secretly without anybody seeing.
Everybody can see exactly what he's doing, going and digging near the [[Ka'bah|كعة]].

So when the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], the other members of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they saw [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] here at the [[Ka'bah|كعة]] digging, they were surprised. "What are you doing?
How can you dig here at the [[Ka'bah|كعة]]? This is not appropriate." They wanted to stop him.
They wanted to stop him. So he said to his son—[[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] said to [[al-Harith|الْحَارِث]], his son—you know, "Go to them and distract them so that they don't stop my work.
Go and argue with them so that I can continue digging. Don't let them stop me."
So [[al-Harith|الْحَارِث]], he went to distract them.
And they started arguing with [[al-Harith|الْحَارِث]], and it was going back and forth while [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] was busy digging, because he knew this is the exact location.
When he dug for a while, finally, he hit a stone. He hit a stone, and it wasn't just any stone.
It was the type of stone that the people would put around the wells.
You know, when people would dig a well, to mark off that location, they would put stones around it. So as he was digging, he finally hit stone.
And the stone was that type of stone that is used to go around a well, so he knew that he was near.
So when he hit that stone, and when he found that stone, he knew what it was. He knew that [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was near, and he said, "[[Allahu Akbar|اللَٜهُ أَكْبَر]]."

And the people of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] who were arguing with the son of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]]—who were still arguing with [[al-Harith|الْحَارِث]] about what his father was doing—they heard [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] say, "[[Allahu Akbar|اللَٜهُ أَكْبَر]]."
And they knew that he's not just saying [[Allahu Akbar|اللَٜهُ أَكْبَر]] for no reason. He must have found something.
So they went to him, and they asked him, "What happened? What are you looking for? What did you find?" He said, "I'm looking for [[Zamzam|زمزم]], and it's here."
And he kept digging, and now they were quiet, because they knew, "Okay, this is really something. He's not just doing this for no reason."
...until he actually found the water, and the water came forward.
So the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] well was rediscovered by [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] after so many centuries, and the water came out.
And they all knew the story of [[Zamzam|زمزم]], so when they saw it come out with their own eyes, they were so happy.
And then he said, "What do you mean, you're my partners? I found it. And this is the responsibility of my family to provide water for the [[hujjaj|حجاج]].
You have no part in this.
And you didn't even want me to dig here, and now that I found it, now you want to be my partners? No, this is not happening."
And then they said to him, "How can you say this is not happening? This is [[Zamzam|زمزم]], you know? This is from the time of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
This is the biggest honor that we can have. How can you take this away from us?
So they were almost going to fight.
And you know how we spoke many times about how the Arabs, over honor, they used to fight and they were ready to die for honor.
So they wanted to fight about this, they were almost getting ready to fight about this as well.
But finally, before the fighting started, they agreed to go to a fortune teller to ask for her advice about what they should do or how they should settle this argument.
And there was a very famous fortune teller in [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
And [[Yathrib|يثرب]], now it is known as [[al-Madinah al-Nabawiyyah|الْمَدِينَة النَّبَوِيَّة]], but at that time it was known as [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
And there was a very famous fortune teller there, she was known as [[Kahinah Bani Sa'd|كاهنة بني سعد]], the fortune teller of [[Banu Sa'd|بنو سعد]].
So they said, "We will go to her. We will go all the way to [[Madinah|مدينة]], and we will ask her what we should do about this argument that we're having.
Does [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] get to have it all for himself and his family, or should the whole [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] share with this honor of the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]?"
They let him continue. And he continued until he actually found the water, and the water came forward.
So the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] well was rediscovered by [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] after so many centuries, and the water came out.
So they agreed. So they went from [[Makkah|مَكَٜة]] to [[Madinah|مدينة]] to consult with [[Kahinah Bani Sa'd|كاهنة بني سعد]], to consult with the fortune teller of [[Banu Sa'd|بنو سعد]].
But when they arrived in [[Madinah|مدينة]], she wasn't there.
And they all knew the story of [[Zamzam|زمزم]], so when they saw it come out with their own eyes, they were so happy.
She was actually on a trip herself. She had traveled to [[Khaybar|خيبر]]. She wasn't in [[Madinah|مدينة]], she had traveled to [[Khaybar|خيبر]]. So they said, "Okay, we will follow her.
We will go to [[Khaybar|خيبر]] as well and we'll meet her there."
And they said to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]], "We are going to share it with you. We are your partners in this." And then he said, "What do you mean, 'You're my partners'?
I found it. And this is the responsibility of my family to provide water for the [[hujjaj|حجاج]]. You have no part in this."
So on the way to [[Khaybar|خيبر]], from [[Madinah|مدينة]] to [[Khaybar|خيبر]], they ran out of water. [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] and his camp, they completely ran out of water.
"And you didn't even want me to dig here, and now that I found it, now you want to be my partners? No, this is not happening."
As for the other people of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they had some water left, but it was very little. It was not much. But [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] and his people, they had nothing.
It was gone.
And then they said to him, "How can you say this is not happening? This is [[Zamzam|زمزم]], you know, this is from the time of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
This is the biggest honor that we can have. How can you take this away from us?

So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] and his camp, they asked those other members of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] to give them some of their water, and they said, "No, we can't give you any water, because we want to live.
You know, if we give you our water—we hardly have any for ourselves—so if we share it with you, we're all going to die. So no, we can't share it with you."
You have no right to have this all for yourself. This is the honor for all of us." And [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] said, "No way. I'm not sharing it with you."
So they were almost going to fight.
And you know how we spoke many times about how the Arabs over honor, they used to fight and they were ready to die for honor.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]]'s camp, they have no water, and the other people of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they're not willing to share their water with them.
So they wanted to fight about this. They were almost getting ready to fight about this as well.
So they consult [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]], "What should we do? We don't have any water, you know, and they're not sharing their water with us, so what should we do?"
But finally, before the fighting started, they agreed to go to a fortune teller to ask for her advice about what they should do or how they should settle this argument.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] said, "Look, it looks like there's no solution to this. It looks like we're all going to die here in the middle of this desert.
Without water, there's no way that we can survive. So to keep some of our honor intact, what we should do is we should all start digging our own graves right now.
And there was a very famous fortune teller in [[Yathrib|يَثْرِب]].

In [[Yathrib|يَثْرِب]]—now it is known as [[al-Madinah al-Nabawiyyah|الْمَدِينَة النَٜبَوِيَٜة]], but at that time it was known as [[Yathrib|يَثْرِب]]—and there was a very famous fortune teller there.
She was known as [[Kahinah Bani Sa'd|كاهنة بني سعد]], the fortune teller of [[Banu Sa'd|بنو سعد]].
We will all dig our own graves, and when one of us dies, the other ones will bury him, so that at the end, at least most of our bodies,
we will be buried, and only the last one who lives, he will remain unburied. That's better than all of these bodies just lying around unburied.
So to keep as much of our honor and dignity as we can, let us dig our own graves, and when the time comes to die, the living ones will bury those who have died."
So they said to him, "Yes, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]], this is a good decision you have made. Let's do it."
So they dug their own graves, each one of them from [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]]'s camp, not from the other members of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], because they still had some water left.
But the other members of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] were watching. They were just looking, "What are they doing?" So they saw them digging their own graves, and they were like, "What?
What's going on here?"
So they dug their own graves, and then they just sat and waited, just waiting to die, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] and his people.
After waiting for some time, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] says, "You know, this is not good. We're just sitting here waiting to die.
This is not an honorable thing to do, just sitting here and not even trying to find a way to survive. We have to at least try to do something.
Let's just get up and look around.
Maybe we will find some water somewhere, rather than just sitting here and waiting for death to come. At least let us try and do something."
So they agreed, "Yes, let's try. We'll try to search for something."
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] gets up, and he gets his camel up as well.

So when the camel of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] gets up, and the camel hits its foot on the ground, some water starts to come right where the foot of the camel of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] steps.
Some water comes out of the ground.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] sees this, and his camp sees this, and they start to drink.
And [[alhamdulillah|الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ]], they're able to drink enough for their needs, and the water is still coming. They have taken care of their thirst, and the water is still coming out.

So then [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَٜلِب]] says to those other people of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] who are against him, and who refused to give them water when they needed it, he says to them, "Come, you drink."
because they hardly had any water left as well.
So he invites them to come and drink from this water as well. So they drink from the water.
And everyone is saved, [[alhamdulillah|الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ]].
And then after everybody drinks, those people from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] who wanted to fight [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] to share the honor of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] with him,
after drinking this water and witnessing what happened here in the middle of the desert, they said to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]],

segments.translit: Wallāhi al-ladhī asqāka al-mā'a fī as-ṣaḥrā', la-huwa al-ladhī asqāka Zamzam. Zamzamu lak. Wallāhi al-ladhī asqāka al-mā'a fī hādhihi as-ṣaḥrā', la-huwa al-ladhī asqāka Zamzam. Zamzamu lak.

segments.text: They said to him, "We swear by Allah, the One who provided you with water here in the middle of this desert, He is the same One who provided you with [[Zamzam|زمزم]].
[[Zamzam|زمزم]] is yours. [[Zamzam|زمزم]] is yours. We're not going to try to fight with you over it anymore."
"This is your right and Allah has made it clear for us now that this is for you and for your family, for you and your descendants."
So the problem was solved. They didn't even have to go to meet the fortune teller that they were going to meet.
It was agreed upon that [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was the caretaker of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] and he had all rights to the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]].
So it remained for [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and his family.
Now when [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], when this whole thing was happening, and when he was first digging that well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] and the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] tried to stop him,
and he sent his son [[al-Harith|الحارث]] to distract them and to stop them from coming, to prevent him from digging,
he thought to himself, "Look, I only have this one son who can help me. [[al-Harith|الحارث]], he's my only son that can help me against these people."
And he felt a weakness because of that, because the Arabs, they used to consider the more sons you have, the more honor you have.
So he felt at this time, "You know, I only have one son who's defending me, one son who is taking care of me, one son who will fight with me.
This is a weakness."
So then he made a vow at that time when he found the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] and the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] came out, he made a vow that:
"O Allah, if You provide me with ten sons, if You give me ten sons, then I will slaughter and sacrifice one of those sons."
"If You provide me with ten sons, I will slaughter one of those sons."
And the reason why he made this vow was because he wanted this honor, and he wanted this power, and he wanted this respect.
And the reason why he said he would slaughter and sacrifice and kill one of his sons was to actually show off that respect that he has to the people.
"Look, I have ten sons.
I have so much power that I can even sacrifice and kill and slaughter one of these sons, and it wouldn't take away from my honor and my respect at all."
This was to show the people what honor you have. "I can kill one of my sons and still, it doesn't make any difference."
It was an evil way, basically, to show their pride and to show their honor that they thought they had to the people.
So he made this vow that if I get ten sons, I will slaughter, sacrifice one of them.
So eventually over time, he did have ten sons. He had exactly ten sons, actually.
And those ten sons were [[al-Abbas|العباس]] and [[Hamzah|حمزة]].

[[al-Abbas|العباس]] and [[Hamzah|حمزة]], they were the only two sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] who actually lived to see Islam, lived to see the Prophet ﷺ's message come, and they believed in him, [[al-Abbas|العباس]] and [[Hamzah|حمزة]].

And then there was [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] and [[Abu Lahab|أبو لهب]]. [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], his real name was [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]]. And [[Abu Lahab|أبو لهب]], his real name was [[Abdul Uzza|عبد العزى]].
But they became known by their [[kunyah|كنية]], [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] and [[Abu Lahab|أبو لهب]].

[[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] and [[Abu Lahab|أبو لهب]] also lived to see the message of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, but they didn't believe in his message and they died upon [[kufr|كفر]], [[wa al-iyadhu billah|والعياذ بالله]].
So these were the only four uncles of the Prophet ﷺ, the four sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] who actually lived to see the message of the Prophet ﷺ.
Two of them believed, and two of them did not believe.

So [[al-Abbas|العباس]] and [[Hamzah|حمزة]], they believed in [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ. And [[Abu Lahab|أبو لهب]] and [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], they didn't believe in [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ and they died upon disbelief.
The other six sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], they did not live to see the message of the Prophet ﷺ.

And those other six sons were [[al-Harith|الحارث]], as we mentioned, who was the first and oldest son, [[al-Zubayr|الزبير]], [[Hajl|حجل]], [[al-Muqawwim|المقوم]], [[Dirar|ضرار]], and the youngest son, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]],
who was the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ. And he actually died even before his son, [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, was born.
So these were the sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], ten sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
The youngest one was the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
And he was the most beloved son to his father. [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] loved [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] more than any of his other sons.
So when they all grew up and you know, they became strong young men,
[[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] remembered his vow that if he got ten sons, he would sacrifice, he would slaughter one of them.
So he decided it was time to fulfill his vow. He decided it was time to fulfill his vow.
So he went to the [[kahin|كاهن]] of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. There was a fortune teller that used to stay right there at the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
Look at the situation how it was, the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] and a fortune teller is sitting right there.
[[alhamdulillah|الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ]] that we have [[tawhid|توحيد]] and that the [[Haramayn|الحرمين]] [[al-Sharifayn|الشريفين]], [[alhamdulillah|الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ]], are places of [[tawhid|توحيد]].
But at that time there was a fortune teller sitting right there at the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he went to this fortune teller of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] and he gave him arrows.
And this was one of the ways that the Arabs of [[Jahiliyyah|جاهلية]], how they used to make decisions to do things.
If they didn't know what type of decision to make, they would write the names on arrows, and then they would throw those arrows, and then they would pick one of the arrows that they had thrown.
This was their way of making decisions.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he took ten arrows, and he wrote the name of each one of his sons on those arrows.
And he told the [[kahin|كاهن]], he told the fortune teller that was there at the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], "Throw these arrows, each one has a name of one of my sons on it, and then select one of the arrows."
"And whoever's name comes out of that arrow, that is the son that I will slaughter, that is the son that I will sacrifice to fulfill the oath that I made."
So the fortune teller, he starts doing it.
He throws the arrows, and while he is throwing it, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] is making [[du'a|دُعَاء]] that, "May it be any of my sons except [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]]."
"May it be any of my sons except my most beloved son [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]]." He really didn't want it to be [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]].
But when the fortune teller threw those arrows and picked up one of them and opened it, guess whose name was on it?
It was [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], of course, he was saddened at this, and this was not the result that he hoped for, but he felt that it was necessary for him to fulfill the vow that he took.

So he took his son, he took him to [[Isaf|إساف]], [[Isaf|إساف]] that idol that was right there in front of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], and he put him down, and he gets ready to slaughter him, to sacrifice him.
And the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they come and they say to him, "Don't do it, O [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]. Don't slaughter your son. Don't sacrifice your son."
He said, "No, I made a vow that I would do it, and I am a man of honor."
"I don't break my vows. I have to do it."
They said, "No no no, you can't do it." They wanted to stop him from doing it. He said, "No, I must do it."
He was very firm in his resolve to slaughter his son to fulfill his vow.
And then they said to him, they said, "O [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], if you do this, this will become a [[sunnah|سنة]] of the Arabs."
"If you do this today, this will become a [[sunnah|سنة]] of the Arabs.
Any one of the Arabs who has ten sons, they will go and they will kill one of their sons, they will slaughter one of their sons."
"And what kind of a tradition do you want to start here? If this starts and if everybody starts doing this, this will really destroy our lives."
He said, "No, I made this vow and I am going to do it."
So this argument went back and forth for some time when finally they agreed. They said, "Okay, we will take a decision from..." from guess who?
[[Kahinah Bani Sa'd|كاهنة]] [[Banu Sa'd|بنو سعد]], from the fortune teller of [[Banu Sa'd|بنو سعد]].
The same fortune teller in [[Yathrib|يثرب]] who they wanted to go to originally when they had the argument about who would get to control [[Zamzam|زمزم]].
So they agreed that, "Okay, we will go to this [[Kahinah Bani Sa'd|كاهنة]], we'll go to this fortune teller of [[Banu Sa'd|بنو سعد]], and we will accept..."
whatever decision she tells us to do. Look at how their lives, you know, revolved around these type of traditions: fortune-telling, soothsaying, all of this type of stuff.
So they agreed, "Okay, we'll go to her, we will consult her, and we will agree to whatever she says."
So they go to [[Kahinah Bani Sa'd|كاهنة بني سعد]], they go to this fortune-telling woman, and they explain to her the situation. And she says to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]],
"What is the [[diyah|دية]]? What is the blood money for someone who is killed?
If somebody is killed and the family of that person who is killed wants the blood money, how much is the blood money that you give?"
They said it is 10 camels. It is 10 camels. She said, "Okay, 10 camels."
"So you have to do the arrow-throwing again." This is what she's telling them.
She said, "On one arrow, put the name of [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]], and on another arrow, put the [[diyah|دية]] of 10 camels.
And throw those two arrows, and then pick up one of the arrows.
If it is the arrow of the 10 camels, then sacrifice 10 camels and [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] is safe.
But if you get the name of [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]], then you have to repeat this process again.
Throw the two arrows again, and if you pick up [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] again, then each time you have to add 10 camels to the previous time.
So the first time if you pick up [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]], then you have to do it again, and you have 10 camels on your account.
If the second time you pick [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] again, you add 10 more camels to that account so it becomes 20.
And keep doing this until you pick the camels, until you pick the camels. And whatever the total amount is at that time, sacrifice that many number of camels."
So they agreed to do this. So they take two arrows: one with the name of [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] and the other with 10 camels.
So they throw the two arrows and they select one. The first time, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]]'s name is selected. So that means 10 camels is there on the account.
They do it again, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]]'s name is selected again. So now 20 camels on the account.
They do it again, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]]'s name comes up again, 30 camels on the account. It keeps going and going and going 10 times.
So there are 100 camels on the account. And then finally, they do it for the 10th time and the camels come up.
So there's a total of 100 camels now, and finally [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]]'s name didn't come on the 10th try, now it is the arrow with the camels.
So upon the agreement, they would sacrifice 100 camels and [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] is free, he's saved.
But [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], after having it nine times go on his son, and then just the last time it went on the camels, he still wasn't sure about this.
He said, "No, I want to try it again just to make sure."
So they do it for an 11th time, and again the camels come up.
Then they do it again, and again the camels come up. So now he sees, "Okay, every time the camels are coming up, so this must be the right decision."
So he agrees to sacrifice 100 camels instead of sacrificing his son [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]]. So [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] was saved.
And that is why the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ used to call himself, "I am the son of two who were going to be sacrificed."
And who are those two?

They are his great-great-grandfather [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], who was almost going to be sacrificed by [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and his own father [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], who was almost going to be slaughtered as well.
So the Prophet ﷺ said, "I am the son of the two who were almost going to be slaughtered."
So this is how the son of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], was saved from being slaughtered.
And eventually he would marry the mother of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], and [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ would be born from that marriage.
And [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], we'll talk more about that next week [[bi-idhnillah|بإذن الله]].

segments.translit: Wallahu a'lam. Wa sallallahu wa sallama wa baraka 'ala nabiyyina Muhammadin wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in.

review.q: What four names were revealed to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] in his consecutive dreams before he was told the well's specific name?
review.a: The dreams commanded him to dig Tibah, Barrah, al-Madmunah, and finally [[Zamzam|زمزم]].

review.q: How was the clue "between intestines and blood" fulfilled when finding the location of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]?
review.a: A cow being sacrificed near the idol [[Isaf|إساف]] broke loose and collapsed, fulfilling the sign of animal remains at the site.

review.q: Who assisted [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] during the excavation of the well and what role did they play?
review.a: His eldest son [[al-Harith|الْحَارِث]] helped him by keeping the opposing [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] members at bay while his father excavated the site.

review.q: Why did [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and the leaders of [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] travel toward [[Yathrib|يَثْرِب]] and [[Khaybar|خيبر]]?
review.a: They intended to seek arbitration from the soothsayer [[Kahinah Bani Sa'd|كاهنة بني سعد]] to resolve their dispute over the ownership of the well.

review.q: What miraculous event occurred in the desert that convinced [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] to grant [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] sole rights to the well?
review.a: A spring of fresh water gushed from beneath the hoof of his camel, which was recognized as a divine sign of his right to custodianship.

review.q: What leadership lesson did the speaker draw from the behavior of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] when his group faced death in the desert?
review.a: The speaker noted that true leadership involves being proactive and resilient during a crisis rather than passively awaiting defeat.

review.q: What was the vow made by [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] during his initial excavation of the well?
review.a: He vowed to sacrifice one of his sons to Allah if he were eventually granted a total of ten sons.

review.q: How was [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] ultimately saved from being sacrificed?
review.a: He was ransomed after casting lots against ten camels at a time until one hundred camels were selected to be slaughtered as [[diyah|دية]].
